record.paper_title: FILTRATIONS BROWNIENNES ET COMPLÉMENTS INDÉPENDANTS : RÉSULTATS ET PROBLÈMES OUVERTS
record.context_brief: Complementability and maximality after the square transform
record.original_question: Let Z = X + iY be a complex Brownian motion started from 0, let R_t = |Z_t|, and define a new complex Brownian motion by Z'_t = ∫_0^t (Z_s / R_s) dZ_s. Let X' and Y' be the real and imaginary parts of Z', so X'_t = ∫_0^t (X_s dX_s - Y_s dY_s)/R_s and Y'_t = ∫_0^t (X_s dY_s + Y_s dX_s)/R_s. Viewing X' or Y' as one-dimensional Brownian motions inside the natural filtration of (X, Y), are they complementable, and are they maximal, where complementable means admitting an independent one-dimensional Brownian complement that together generates the same filtration as (X, Y), and maximal means that their generated filtration cannot be strictly enlarged by another one-dimensional Brownian motion from the same ambient filtration? The source notes that the answers are the same for X' and Y'.

evidence.quote: Les parties réelle et imaginaire de Z0 sont les mouvements browniens donnés par X0t = R t 0 XsdXs − YsdYs / Rs et Y0t = R t 0 XsdYs + YsdXs / Rs.

On dit que X0 est complémentable dans F(X,Y)· s’il existe un brownien linéaire Y0 dans F(X,Y)·, indépendant de X0 et tel que (X0, Y0) engendre F(X,Y)·. On dit que X0 est maximal dans F(X,Y)· si pour tout brownien linéaire X00 dans F(X,Y)·, l’inclusion FX0· ⊂ FX00· entraîne l’égalité FX0· = FX00·.

La question de savoir si les mouvements browniens X0 et Y0 sont complémentables ou non, maximaux ou non, semble encore plus délicate. On peut toutefois noter que les réponses sont les mêmes pour les deux browniens.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Z=(Z_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be a standard complex Brownian motion started at $0$, written as $Z_t=X_t+iY_t$ with $X,Y$ independent real Brownian motions, and let $R_t=|Z_t|$. Define the complex-valued process
$$Z'_t=\int_0^t \frac{Z_s}{R_s}\,dZ_s,$$
which is itself a complex Brownian motion started at $0$. Write $Z'_t=X'_t+iY'_t$, so that
$$X'_t=\int_0^t \frac{X_s\,dX_s-Y_s\,dY_s}{R_s},\qquad Y'_t=\int_0^t \frac{X_s\,dY_s+Y_s\,dX_s}{R_s}.$$
Both $X'$ and $Y'$ are one-dimensional Brownian motions adapted to the natural (completed, right-continuous) filtration $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}_\cdot$ of $(X,Y)$.

Say that a linear Brownian motion $B$ in $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}_\cdot$ is:
- **complementable** in $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}_\cdot$ if there exists a linear Brownian motion $C$ adapted to $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}_\cdot$ such that $B$ and $C$ are independent and the pair $(B,C)$ generates the filtration $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}_\cdot$;
- **maximal** in $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}_\cdot$ if for every linear Brownian motion $B''$ adapted to $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}_\cdot$, the inclusion $\mathcal F^{B}_\cdot \subset \mathcal F^{B''}_\cdot$ implies $\mathcal F^{B}_\cdot = \mathcal F^{B''}_\cdot$.

Determine whether $X'$ (equivalently $Y'$) is complementable in $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}_\cdot$, and whether it is maximal in $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}_\cdot$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of complementability and maximality of the real and imaginary parts of the iterated complex Brownian motion $Z'=\int (Z_s/R_s)dZ_s$ inside the filtration of $(X,Y)$ is described as a delicate open question in the surveys on Brownian filtrations; related results on maximal Brownian motions (Brossard–Leuridan, Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré 2009) develop the general framework but do not resolve this specific case. No subsequent publication resolving it was located.

status_evidence.title: Maximal Brownian motions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses complementability and maximality for linear Brownian motions inside a planar Brownian filtration, providing general criteria but not resolving the specific case of Z' = ∫(Z/R)dZ.
status_evidence.claim: General framework exists but the specific case is not addressed as solved.

status_evidence.title: On certain almost Brownian filtrations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies subtle examples of Brownian filtrations and their complements, illustrating the delicacy of these questions.
status_evidence.claim: Related questions remain open in the literature.
